## Step 4 & 5 — Per-Perspective Checklists & Findings

### Perspective 4: Auditory Access
**WCAG Criteria:** 1.2.1, 1.2.2, 1.2.3, 1.2.5, 1.4.2 | **Red Flags:** None triggered

| Checklist Item | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<video>` with speech has `<track kind="captions">` with valid `src` | PASS | `<track kind="captions" src="/video/tutorial-en.vtt" ... />` present. |
| Media player controls keyboard-operable | PASS | Native `<button>` and `<input type="range">` elements handle all interactions. |
| No audio auto-plays / immediate pause control | PASS | `autoPlay={false}` enforced in JSX. |
| Caption accuracy & timing | FINDING | Content-level boundary. Cannot verify from source. |
| Transcript includes speaker identification | FINDING | Content-level boundary. Cannot verify from source. |

**Finding:** Caption accuracy, timing, and speaker identification cannot be verified from source code. Requires content author review to ensure alignment with WCAG 1.2.2 and 1.2.1.
**WCAG:** 1.2.2 (Captions), 1.2.1 (Transcript)
**Perspective:** Auditory Access
**Severity:** MINOR
**Route to:** Content Author (secondary: Front-End Dev)
**Evidence:** `<track kind="captions" src="/video/tutorial-en.vtt" />` and `<details>` transcript present in JSX.
**Fix:** [Human verification required — cannot be confirmed from source]

### Perspective 6: Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**WCAG Criteria:** 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 2.4.2, 2.4.4, 2.4.6, 3.1.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2, 4.1.3 | **Red Flags:** None triggered

| Checklist Item | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Landmark regions & heading hierarchy | PASS | `<section aria-label="Video player">` + `<h2>` provide logical structure. Page shell supplies `<main>`. |
| DOM order matches visual reading order | PASS | Video → Controls → Transcript follows visual flow. |
| Form inputs have visible `<label>` | FINDING | Labels use `.sr-only` class. WCAG 1.3.1 permits programmatic association, but the checklist explicitly requires *visible* labels for cognitive accessibility and reduced AT dependency. |
| Custom widgets use correct ARIA roles/states | PASS | `role="toolbar"` correctly groups controls. `aria-pressed`, `aria-valuetext`, and `aria-label` follow APG patterns. |
| Status messages use `aria-live` appropriately | PASS | Time display uses `aria-live="off"`, correctly suppressing constant updates that would disrupt screen reader users. |

**Finding:** Form input labels for seek and volume sliders are visually hidden via `.sr-only`. While WCAG 1.3.1 allows programmatically associated hidden labels, the JTBD checklist explicitly requires visible labels. Hidden labels increase cognitive load and reduce accessibility for non-screen-reader users.
**WCAG:** 3.3.2 (Labels in Words), 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships)
**Perspective:** Screen Reader & Semantic Structure
**Severity:** MINOR
**Route to:** UX Design (primary: label strategy/interaction design) (secondary: Content Author)
**Evidence:** `<label className="sr-only" htmlFor="seek-slider">Seek</label>` in JSX; `.sr-only` CSS class applies `clip: rect(0,0,0,0)` and absolute positioning.
**Fix:** Replace `.sr-only` labels with visible inline labels or visually styled label elements adjacent to the range inputs. Justify hidden labels only if UX research confirms they degrade the visual hierarchy or mobile layout.

---

The `.sr-only` label pattern should be replaced with visible labels for broader accessibility, and content authors must verify caption/transcript accuracy against the video asset. No CRITICAL or MAJOR barriers detected; infrastructure is solid and APG-compliant.
